guides.author: Michael Hodges
guides.imageAlt: A marina used for Guide publication testing

sections.heading: Approach and arrival
body: The approach paragraph is deliberately descriptive rather than navigational advice. It establishes current public rendering while avoiding invented safety facts. The berth paragraph adds sufficient editorial substance for the current Guide threshold. The facilities paragraph confirms only that this is disposable test content. The final paragraph proves the record is server rendered and available through the normal Guide route after publication. Additional editorial words make the fixture comfortably exceed the existing publication threshold without asserting depths, tides, hazards, coordinates, radio channels, berth availability or any other fact that a skipper might mistake for current navigation guidance. This record exists only inside a temporary test directory and has no connection to production content.

guides.title: CMS Noindex Characterisation Guide
guides.summary: A disposable published Guide with an explicit noindex override.
guides.introduction: This published but excluded Guide contains enough editorial copy to remain publicly readable while proving that its explicit noindex setting removes it from sitemap eligibility without changing the behavior of other Guide records.
guides.author: Michael Hodges
guides.imageAlt: A harbour artwork reference retained during Guide testing

sections.heading: Overview
body: This temporary test record is intentionally noindexed. Its paragraphs supply sufficient content for current publication validation while making no navigation claims. It must remain available over HTTP, keep its canonical link, and remain absent from sitemap results. Existing published Guides and stories must stay unaffected throughout these checks. Further neutral copy keeps the fixture beyond the existing publication threshold while avoiding invented facilities, coordinates, tides, depths, hazards or VHF information. The record belongs only to a disposable test store and must never be treated as a real harbour Guide or copied into production data.
